A patient journey through linked records

This invented case follows diagnosis, eligibility, baseline evidence, treatment, dosimetry, safety review, course completion and later treatment. The compact example contains two cycles in its initial course and a distinct retreatment course; it does not prescribe a regimen.

What the relationships let you ask

The revised outcome framework

All 94 revised spreadsheet elements are mapped. Their framework dimension, variable role, priority, unit of analysis, timing, validation status and revision notes are preserved. The paper contributes 65 traceable table occurrences, including aliases and paper-only candidates.

Core, Recommended and Exploratory are source priorities. They do not establish clinical approval, a validated core outcome set, or required data for every record.

Definition changes and remaining decisions

  • Early PSA rise is recorded without presuming flare or excluding progression.
  • RECIP molecular response, PCWG progression and exploratory uptake changes remain distinct.
  • Whole-body tumor volume is separated from single-lesion ROI measurements.
  • Clinician CTCAE, PRO-CTCAE items, pain and physical function have separate records and evidence.
  • Planned completion, first progression, NLCB and later treatment are different events.
  • The review log flags remaining RECIP OR-versus-AND wording, PCWG4 release-specific rules, signed best-response wording and legacy dose-threshold language.

A proposed extension of the deployed MIDRC dictionary

Baseline: 1.4.3-2-g7505333, commit 7505333d56c87a289463a814131e38d0f2be6674, retrieved 16 October 2026. This file is an offline review tool, not the MIDRC portal or a deployed Gen3 release.

Earlier structureVersion 0.3Why
imaging_series + image_filept_series_file, nm_series_file, ct_series_file, mr_series_fileUse MIDRC’s modality-specific file records, identifiers, definitions and constraints.
laboratory_result, roi_measurement, anthropometric_assessmentmeasurement profilesReuse test_result_number and add units, coded identity and evidence context.
lifestyle_assessmentobservation profileOne dated observation using observation_name and observation_answer.
segmentation; segmentation_fileannotation; dicom_annotation_file or annotation_fileKeep the contour execution and its binary artifact distinct.
raw_imaging_file; clinical_document_filesupplementary_fileReuse existing file-index metadata. A radiology report can use radiology_report when its structure fits.

Preserve constraints rather than silently widen them

Existing required fields, enums, array types and link groups remain intact. Legacy test-name and procedure-name enums remain intact: new coded/source identity fields carry other values. Existing CT pixel spacing and PT slice thickness remain arrays. Seven enum additions are explicitly proposed for annotation workflow names and RTDOSE; no baseline values are removed.

PT and NM

PT means PET. NM covers planar and SPECT; the new optional nm_acquisition_kind distinguishes them. Hybrid PET/CT and SPECT/CT use separate PT/NM and CT file records linked to their examination. PT’s existing ct_images Boolean is retained; it does not replace CT file metadata.

Templates are editing aids

Required keys use the supplied portal style, such as *submitter_id. Remove the asterisk before submission, fill required values and remove unfilled optionals. Required alternative link groups still require at least one member even when individual links are unstarred. The attached PT/NM templates included urls, which is absent from the deployed schemas; the expanded node templates omit it and provide a separate file-index manifest.

Validation and next integration step

Local checks cover all 67 schemas against JSON Schema and the deployed Gen3 metaschema, 29 baseline regression fixtures, 122 connected synthetic records, the additive-patch round trip, source coverage and 27 negative cases. The second-cycle dose summary explicitly marks its source evidence as partial. A receiving Gen3 build and staging submission remain necessary. Review the patch and collection profiles before adapting the production dictionary.

Node changes

29 baseline nodes are retained: 17 receive optional additions and 12 are unchanged. There are 38 proposed theranostics nodes. Keeping unrelated baseline nodes preserves existing MIDRC content; the count does not mean all 67 are required for every patient.

MIDRC dictionary · MIDRC source repository

Structure, definitions and meaning work together

The data model, dictionary and semantic layer are complementary. In Gen3, one executable dictionary contains both node relationships and property definitions; the graph, tables and JSON here are generated from that same schema. The independent terminology and ontology resources give the recorded concepts shared meaning.

ComponentWhat it specifiesLu177-PSMA example
Data modelRecord types, identity, relationships, cardinalities and time context.Dose D1 references lesion L1 and calculation run R1. L1 references patient P1. R1 references cycle C1, acquisitions and contours.
Data dictionaryEach field’s definition, data type, permissible values, units and validation constraints.absorbed_dose_gy is numeric in Gy; the statistic and uncertainty must be explicit. measurement.test_result_number contains the numeric result.
TerminologyStandard identifiers, preferred names, synonyms and controlled value sets.LOINC 2857-1 identifies PSA mass concentration in serum/plasma when that assay meaning matches. The number 42 and unit ng/mL are separate from its code.
OntologyFormally defined concepts and semantic relationships, such as kinds of measurements, anatomy and processes.A proposed semantic binding can relate the dose property to an absorbed-dose concept and its target to an anatomical concept. The exact NucLex/RadLex identifiers and relations require ontology-owner review.

These categories can overlap

A terminology can be organized as an ontology. LOINC is a structured terminology for observations and has ontology-related products; RadLex is an ontology as well as a radiology vocabulary. NucLex supplies the developing nuclear-medicine ontology. These resources are not three interchangeable code lists, and the local data model does not redefine them.

Two different kinds of relationship

D1 → L1 is a link between this patient’s records. A conceptual relation such as a measurement being about an anatomical structure is a semantic assertion governed by an ontology. A foreign key does not automatically assert an ontology relationship, and assigning a concept code does not supply the missing patient, cycle or image links.

A complete PSA example

Store the measured value once in a measurement record with units, assay identity and specimen context. Link it to its laboratory_panel and patient. A response_assessment.baseline_psa_results link identifies its baseline role; a separate confirmation link identifies a later sample. The response calculation retains its criteria and version. The same PSA code can apply to both samples: their different roles come from the model.

How to govern the layers

Keep stable field names and record identifiers separate from preferred labels. Record model, dictionary and terminology/ontology release versions independently. Curate candidate mappings as exact, broader, narrower or related only after review. NucLex IDs are left unset until verified. Changing a label need not change the model; changing meaning, type, unit, cardinality or record grain may require a migration.

What the layers do not decide

The model records the physician’s eligibility, continuation, adjustment and completion decisions with their evidence. It does not generate a personalized treatment prescription. Generic JSON validation also does not establish clinical completeness or validate every CTCAE, RECIP or PCWG rule.
